newsitem.title: USA: Edgar Bronfman named to Swiss Holocaust Fund board.
newsitem.headline: Edgar Bronfman named to Swiss Holocaust Fund board.

text.p: World Jewish Congress head Edgar Bronfman, who led the fight over unclaimed Jewish assets in Switzerland, was named on Wednesday to temporarily take a seat on the new Swiss Fund to aid Holocaust survivors.

The executive board of the World Jewish Restitution Organisation (WJRO), which Bronfman also leads, made the decision after Nobel Peace Prize winner Elie Wiesel resigned from the seven-member Fund board, citing statements "made in the Swiss press."
Wiesel, who had also been named international chairman of the Fund, bowed out after Swiss officials said his additional title would carry no power.
WJC sources said there had been difficulty finding a permanent replacement as many potential candidates felt Wiesel had been insulted.
Four of the fund's members are named by the Swiss government and three by the WJRO, which is a branch of the WJC.

WJC Executive Director Elan Steinberg said Bronfman would serve only on an interim basis until a permanent replacement was found. He said he expected that a replacement would be named at a WJRO meeting in Jerusalem on June 2.
"Mr Bronfman was asked to serve now so that the fund can begin its work," he said.

Jewish sources said several guidelines have been set for the $190 million Fund that was set up with donations from Swiss banks and industries after a spate of international cirticism over the Swiss role in the Second World War as bankers for the Third Reich.
The sources said that about 500,000 survivors would be eligible for money from the fund and that need would be the prime criterion rather than extent of suffering.
Germany has come under criticism from Jewish groups for basing some reparation payments on the length of time a survivor spent in a concentration camp or a ghetto.
